svg.title: Something happened between the READ and the WRITE
svg.desc: Two thread timelines interleaved: thread A reads 5, thread B reads 5, both add one, both write 6, and the shared counter ends at 6 instead of 7 — one update lost. Below, the same sequence held by a lock runs uninterrupted while B is blocked and the counter reaches 7. A two-lock deadlock cycle is drawn beside its fix of a fixed lock order, and a producer-queue-consumer design removes the shared state entirely.
svg.text: Something happened between the READ and the WRITE
two threads, one counter, six steps
the bug is not the addition. It is that something
happened between the READ and the WRITE.
the same two threads, with a lock
fix: everyone takes L1 before L2
counter += 1 is atomic, I tested it
Queue put+get 654.7 ns vs bare lock 24.9 ns
